newsitem.title: HONG KONG: New Hong Kong leader to pay income tax.
newsitem.headline: New Hong Kong leader to pay income tax.

text.p: Hong Kong's future leader, billionaire Tung Chee-hwa, is making a clean break with another British colonial tradition by submitting his official pay to the mercy of the territory's taxmen.
Tung's office said on Tuesday that he would pay income tax on his salary and perks after he takes over as the territory's chief executive at midnight on June 30.
Tung, chosen by a Chinese-assembled committee last December, would earn around HK$300,000 (US40,000) a month, the same as outgoing British Governor Chris Patten. But Patten enjoyed a tax-free status.
The rationale for the decision on Tung's own tax status was that he was a "local person" and thus liable to pay the same taxes as his fellow citizens, a statement from his office said.
The post-colonial leader earlier announced he would not be moving into Government House, the official residence of colonial governors, but would stay in the comfort of his own home.
